title: Point any OpenAI-compatible app at Nerva as its backend
contract: The api_server platform serves `POST /v1/chat/completions` (system messages flattened into an ephemeral prompt, last message as input, the rest as history, a conversation fingerprint deriving a stable session id for stateless frontends, streaming SSE plus a custom `hermes.tool.progress` event, idempotency keys, 502 with `agent_incomplete` rather than rendering a failure string as content), `POST /v1/responses` with server-side storage, `previous_response_id` chaining, named conversations and spec-compliant typed streaming events, `GET|DELETE /v1/responses/{id}`, `GET /v1/models` advertising a stable virtual model plus route aliases, and `GET /api/model/options` returning the native provider inventory (acp-mcp-dev.api-chat-completions, .api-responses, .api-get-response, .api-delete-response, .api-models, .api-model-options).
governance: inbound requests are untrusted and must be marked tainted at the boundary so the kernel's taint escalation forces mutating kinds to the approval queue; mandatory bearer key even on loopback; default-off flag; bind 127.0.0.1.

title: Accept work from another agent over the open A2A protocol
contract: The full Linux-Foundation A2A v1.0 inbound surface on stdlib HTTP: a signed Agent Card at `/.well-known/agent-card.json` (plus the legacy path) with skills derived from enabled toolsets and a public URL resolved from forwarded headers; one JSON-RPC endpoint accepting both v1.0 PascalCase and pre-1.0 path-style names for SendMessage, SendStreamingMessage (JSON-RPC-enveloped SSE), GetTask, ListTasks, CancelTask, SubscribeToTask and four push-notification-config methods; eight task states with terminal-state handling; `[INPUT_REQUIRED]` replies flipping a task to INPUT_REQUIRED so the peer knows to answer; HMAC-SHA256-signed push webhooks with SSRF filtering of the callback URL; and inbound tasks injected into the *live* gateway session so a peer gets the same agent, memory and tools (acp-mcp-dev.a2a-plugin, .a2a-agent-card, .a2a-jsonrpc, .a2a-send-message, .a2a-send-streaming, .a2a-get-task, .a2a-list-tasks, .a2a-cancel-task, .a2a-subscribe-task, .a2a-push-create/-get/-list/-delete, .a2a-health, .a2a-metrics, .a2a-conversations).
governance: inbound peer requests are external and tainted; an approved task's execution still crosses whatever kernel kind the work implies. The approval floor is the differentiator here and must not be traded away for protocol conformance.

- The A2A v1.0 JSON-RPC surface (SendMessage, SendStreamingMessage, GetTask, ListTasks, CancelTask, SubscribeToTask, push-config methods)
- Task states including INPUT_REQUIRED, streaming SSE, signed push webhooks
- Agent Card at the standard /.well-known/agent-card.json path with skills
- Executing an approved task in a live session and returning the result to the peer

title: Call other agents as tools and fan work out to peers
contract: Five outbound tools registered independently of the inbound listener, so an agent can call peers without exposing itself: `a2a_discover` (fetch and summarise a remote Agent Card before calling), `a2a_call` (natural-language task to a configured peer name or a raw URL, returning the context id for multi-turn), `a2a_list`, `a2a_history` (recall a persisted transcript by context id, surviving compaction and restarts), and `a2a_orchestrate` (fan out by capability tag with all/first/best aggregation). Peers live in an `a2a_agents:` registry with url, bearer auth, timeout and capability tags (acp-mcp-dev.a2a-tool-discover, .a2a-tool-call, .a2a-tool-list, .a2a-tool-history, .a2a-tool-orchestrate, .a2a-agents-config).
governance: calling a peer sends the owner's data off the box: it is egress and must cross the existing plugin.egress kernel path with the egress ledger, per-peer allowlisting, and outbound credential redaction before the text leaves.

title: Harden the A2A channel against a hostile or runaway peer
contract: Identity derived from the presented credential and never from the body, constant-time compared, with per-peer tokens so rate limiting and audit are meaningful; a bind-host safety rule where a token alone does not widen the bind and a wide host alone is ignored (two independent switches); an optional trusted-peer allow-list layered above authentication; inbound text defanged (eight injection patterns neutralised to `[filtered]`, never rejected) and framed with an explicit untrusted-provenance banner, applied to *every* message including ones starting with `/` so a peer can never reach operator slash commands; outbound credential redaction (eight patterns incl. JWTs and emails); 60 req/min per identity; a per-context ping-pong turn cap of 5 with a hard ceiling of 20; and a JSONL audit line per exchange (acp-mcp-dev.a2a-auth, .a2a-bind, .a2a-trusted-peers, .a2a-inbound-filter, .a2a-outbound-redaction, .a2a-rate-limit, .a2a-turn-cap, .a2a-audit, .a2a-env).
governance: read-only filters guarding a privileged path; the audit line should join the existing hash-chained audit rather than a separate JSONL, so a peer exchange is provable alongside every other action.

- Inbound injection defanging and an untrusted-provenance banner, for when peer text reaches a model
- Outbound credential redaction
- Per-identity rate limiting and an anti-loop turn cap
- Bind-host safety rule and a trusted-peer allow-list separate from authentication
- A dedicated append-only A2A audit line per exchange

title: Let third-party apps ride the owner's authenticated model subscription
contract: `hermes proxy start` runs a local OpenAI-compatible forwarder that replaces the client's Authorization header with a freshly-resolved bearer from an OAuth-authenticated provider, so any app can point at it with any token. Deliberately minimal — it never logs, transforms or rewrites bodies — with a per-adapter allowlist of forwarded paths (404 otherwise), hop-by-hop header stripping, a one-shot retry on upstream 401/429 via a credential pool, streaming preserved chunk-by-chunk, an authentication check before the port is bound, and two adapters (Nous Portal, xAI OAuth) behind a five-member ABC (acp-mcp-dev.proxy-root, .proxy-start, .proxy-status, .proxy-providers, .proxy-server, .proxy-adapter-api, .proxy-adapter-nous, .proxy-adapter-xai).
governance: would be an unmediated egress path by design — bodies opaque, no ledger entry, no kernel hop. That is the reason to decline it.
historical_exclusion_reason: It is a credential-lending service, not an agent capability, and it inverts the product's central promise: a proxy that attaches the owner's real credentials to a request it has explicitly decided not to inspect is an ungoverned egress path with a listening socket, sitting next to a kernel whose entire job is that no privileged effect escapes unmediated. The overlap with the OpenAI-compatible inbound API is also real — that row gives external apps a Nerva-shaped front door where taint and the queue apply, which is the version of this idea that fits.
